newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dollar significantly undervalued - BoF's Marchelli.
newsitem.headline: Dollar significantly undervalued - BoF's Marchelli.

text.p: Bank of France monetary policy council member Paul Marchelli reaffirmed on Wednesday that the dollar was significantly undervalued against European currencies.
In an interview with Reuters, Marchelli said he was speaking in a personal capacity and Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet was responsible for giving the official position.
"All European currencies have a problem in relation to the dollar. The dollar is significantly undervalued against Euorpean currencies," he said.
It would be a good start if the dollar were to rise above 5.50 francs, compared with 5.24 today.
"If we go beyond a level of 5.50 francs that would be a good start. Below that red line, we are dealing with a currency which is cheating," he said.
Marchelli, one of nine members of the Bank of France's monetary policy council, said in late November that the dollar was undervalued against European currencies.
French officials have repeatedly called for a rise in the dollar, which Prime Minister Alain Juppe has described as chronically undervalued.

Asked on Wednesday how he thought France should go about achieving its desire for a stronger dollar, Marchelli said the best way would be to press ahead with plans for monetary union in 1999 to strengthen Europe's hand in pushing its case.
"We must launch the euro within the planned timetable," he said.
But he said he saw no reason to devalue the franc.

Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing suggested last month that France might have to reconsider a decade-old link between the franc and the mark if it could not get joint action with Germany to achieve a stronger dollar.
